column2: req_desc

Sign in without revealing accounts
Sign-in accepts a seeded email and password, starts a session, and answers both a wrong password and an unknown email with the identical 401 response from API.

Sessions and sign-out
Every API route except sign-in and health requires a session, the current-person route returns the signed-in person, and sign-out ends the session at once.

Documents
A signed-in person lists the documents shared with them and creates a new empty document that they own, with the name rules in API.

Tables and typed columns
The Owner creates tables and Text, Decimal, Date, Bool, Reference and Formula columns, renames columns and changes data column types, with the validation stated in API.

Typed cell values
Each cell write is validated against its column type and read from its exact decimal text, never through binary floating point, then stored and displayed in the canonical form from Business rules.

Cell revisions
Every cell write carries the cell's revision, and a stale revision gets the 409 response from API with the cell's current value and changes nothing.

One winner per cell
Of two or more simultaneous writes carrying the same revision of one cell, exactly one succeeds and every other gets the stale-revision 409.

Formula language
Formula columns evaluate the literals, operators, references and traversals defined in Business rules for every row.

Error values
Formula failures produce one of the five error values under the rules in Business rules, an error propagates to every dependent cell, and IFERROR never catches #CIRC!.

Circular formulas
A formula change that creates a cycle through one or more formulas saves, and every cell on the cycle and every cell depending on it shows #CIRC! whatever else it would show.

Recalculation in the same request
Every edit, paste, rename, undo and redo recalculates every dependent cell in every table and summary in the same request and transaction, evaluating each cell once, so the response and any later read agree.

Ordered recalculation list
Every edit response carries the recalculation list of changed cells with their dependency depth, in the order, with the counts, stacks, access, document revision and sentence, defined in API and Business rules.

Summary tables
The Owner creates a summary of a table grouped by one to three columns, with one group row per distinct key as keyed in Business rules, its Count, and the Sum of each chosen column.

Totals current after every row change
Adding, editing, pasting or deleting rows updates summary group rows, their Count and Sums, and every aggregate formula in the response to that same request.

Deleting a row
Deleting a row turns every Reference cell that pointed at it into #REF! and every formula that followed those references into #REF!.

Deleting a column
Deleting a column turns every formula that names it into #NAME?, and a column used by a summary or as the row owner cannot be deleted, as qualified in Business rules.

Personal undo and redo
Each person has their own undo and redo stacks per document, bounded as stated in Business rules, in which a pasted block or cleared range is one entry, and an undo never reverts anyone else's edit.

Exact restore of a deleted row
Undoing a row deletion restores the row in its place with its cells and revision, every reference still broken by that deletion, every formula that had turned #REF!, and every summary group it removed.

Restore of a deleted column
Undoing a column deletion restores the column in its position with all its values, and every formula that had turned #NAME? evaluates again, also when that undo follows the undo of a later rename.

Undo conflicts
An undo or redo whose target was changed since by anything other than that person's own later undos and redos gets a 409, changes nothing and drops that entry, and undo or redo on an empty stack gets a 409.

Role permissions enforced by the server
The server refuses every action a role may not take with 403 and changes nothing, so a Viewer cannot edit a cell, paste, add or delete a row, change a formula, rename, undo or redo.

Row access rules
The Owner marks a Text column as a table's row owner, and a member shared with own-row scope sees and reaches only the rows whose owner cell is their email.

Restricted views on totals and summaries
For a member with own-row scope, aggregate formulas, summary groups, row counts, the recalculation list and CSV exports are computed from their visible rows only, and they match that member's grid and API rows.

Rows under own-row scope
A member with own-row scope gets their email in the owner cell of every row they add and cannot assign a row to anyone else.

Sharing a document
The Owner shares a document with any valid email address as Editor or Viewer with a row scope, and the status and body are identical whether or not the address has an account.

Invite email
Each share action sends at most one invite email to exactly one recipient, holding the sharer's name, the document name, the role and the document link and nothing else.

Invite outage and Resend
A share made while mail is unreachable is saved as Not sent, and once mail is reachable Resend sends exactly one invite without a server restart.

Storage-confirmed exports
An export becomes Ready with a download only after object storage confirms the stored file's byte size and SHA-256, and an export request refused as cross-site creates no export record.

CSV format
Exports are RFC 4180 CSV with CRLF line endings, a header row, values exactly as displayed and rows in insertion order.

Text neutralised in CSV
Values of text origin that start with one of the six characters listed in Business rules are exported with a leading apostrophe, while the grid and API keep the value as typed.

Export with storage down
When object storage is unreachable an export ends Failed with no download, and grid editing keeps working.

Formula preview
The preview endpoint evaluates an unsaved formula against one row in the caller's view and returns its display, its error diagnosis or its located reading diagnosis without saving anything.

Error order and shape
Every API error uses the single JSON error shape and the precedence stated in API, and a request with several faults answers the first matching step and changes nothing.

Health and boot with services down
The health route answers 200 at all times, the app starts and serves while mail or storage is unreachable, and it recovers when they return without a restart.

Server boundary
The server rejects cross-origin writes, oversized bodies and non-JSON bodies as stated in Server boundary, and never serves source files or credentials.

Seed data
On first start against an empty database, the app creates exactly the accounts, document, tables, rows, summary and shares listed in Seed data.

Workspace at 1280
At 1280 by 800 the workspace shows the table rail, the pinned formula bar, the grid with sticky header row and first column, and the status bar, with no page-level horizontal scroll.

Workspace at 768
At 768 by 1024 the workspace shows the grid with a collapsible table rail and the status bar, and no pinned formula bar.

Record cards at 375
At 375 by 812 each row is a record card, tables are switched from a drawer, dialogs open as full-height sheets, and no grid is shown.

Touch targets
Every control in the 375 record view and its sheets meets the touch size stated in Visual design.

Grid keyboard model
The grid works from the keyboard alone with the navigation keys, focus rules and grid attributes in Interactions, including the undo and redo shortcuts from anywhere in the workspace.

Column options menu
A column header's options menu opens from its header button or from the active cell by the keys in Interactions, is operated by arrow keys, returns focus to its header button on close, and stays fully inside the viewport above the status bar.

Dialog focus
Every dialog, sheet and the table drawer keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the control named in Interactions.

Formula live preview
Typing in the formula bar or a formula dialog updates its preview on each keystroke without reloading the grid or moving focus, shows only the reply for the newest text, and announces the settled preview once after the typing pause stated in Interactions.

Settle roll
After each successful commit, changed cells animate in dependency order with the roll, crossfade and stamp timings in Motion and effects, and end on the stored display.

Recalculation markers and rail badges
Every changed visible cell carries its server depth in a data-recalc-depth attribute, and every table not on screen shows a badge with its changed-cell count, until the next successful commit.

Status bar tally
The status bar counts up to the number of changed cells and ends on the recalculation sentence.

Reduced motion
Under reduced motion, followed live without a reload, values swap instantly, sheets and leaving cards do not move, and changed cells keep a static accent or error bar, while badges, markers, the sentence and announcements stay the same.

Live announcements
Each commit announces the recalculation sentence politely, even when it repeats the previous one, only the newest-sent of several commits applied together is announced, and conflicts, circular results, hidden rows and lost permission are announced assertively with the copy in Feedback states.

Published copy verbatim
Every string in Feedback states renders and is announced character for character.

Journey: Owner sets up a ledger
The Owner creates a document, a table with typed and formula columns, rows and a summary, renames a column and the table, and adds a column from a full-height sheet at 375 by 812, entirely in the browser, as in journey 1.

Journey: Editor enters orders
An Editor enters orders from the keyboard alone, keeps committing while an earlier save is slow, selects, clears and pastes quantities, survives a lost response and a dropped connection, and corrects with undo while totals settle, on the grid and on record cards, as in journey 2.

Journey: Editors resolve conflicts
Two people race on one cell, one row, one formula and a rename against a formula, and each race ends in its published outcome with the loser seeing and hearing the current state, as in journey 3.

Journey: Editor deletes and restores a product
An Editor deletes a product row, finds it gone from the picker and counts, and undoes it so every reference, formula, summary group and picker option returns, then deletes and restores an order from the deleted-row status on a phone, as in journey 4.

Journey: Owner shares and resends
The Owner has an unsafe address refused, shares during a mail outage, sees Not sent, and later resends one invite, as in journey 5.

Journey: Owner exports for the accountant
The Owner exports Customers by keyboard, hears each status once, downloads the same neutralised stored file before and after later edits, keeps the refusal copy for a damaged file, uses the Exports sheet on a phone, and sees the failure path when storage is down, as in journey 6.

Journey: Viewer reads and downloads
A Viewer signs in from a workspace link, returns to it, reads the document read-only, downloads a summary CSV that matches the screen and signs out, as in journey 7.

Journey: Editor counts stock on a phone
An Editor with own-row scope updates a stock count from a record card at 375 by 812, sees restricted totals settle, sees the scope widened and narrowed on the next action, loses write access without a reload and regains it, as in journey 8.

Ledger look
The workspace reads as a paper ledger as described in Visual design, with hairline-ruled rows, serif table names, mono numbers aligned on the decimal point and a single cobalt accent.

Server-owned data and credentials
Service credentials and URLs come only from the environment, and all document state, recalculation and access decisions are made on the server against the real services.

Formula functions and date arithmetic
Formulas evaluate SUM, COUNT, SUMBY, COUNTBY, MIN, MAX, AVERAGE, ROUND, IF, IFERROR and date arithmetic over the caller's visible rows with the argument, blank and error rules in Business rules.

Column rename rewrites formulas
Renaming a column rewrites every formula token and summary name that names it, leaves every other character byte for byte, and one Undo restores the old texts exactly.

Paste a block
Pasting a block of cells writes them all or none in one request with one recalculation and one undo entry, as qualified in API and Interactions.

Honest optimistic commit
A pending commit shows its new value muted and busy without holding back later commits, and a failed one, after the single resend stated in Interactions, returns the cell, row and rail to their earlier state with no roll, no markers and no phantom row.

Column revisions
Every column change carries the column's revision, a stale one gets the 409 from API and changes nothing, and of simultaneous changes with one revision exactly one wins, whether made from the formula bar or a dialog.

Linearisable document edits
Parallel edits to one document apply one at a time, so the recalculation lists for a shared aggregate form one chain ending at the stored value and parallel row adds take distinct positions.

Landing and announcement after create
Creating a document, table, column or summary waits for the server's answer, then moves to the published address and focus target and announces the creation once in Workspace status, and Back and reload keep each landed address.

A deleted row is gone everywhere
Until it is undone, a deleted row is absent from reads, writes, the Reference picker, aggregates, formula preview, rail counts and new exports, and Undo brings it back under the same id.

Simultaneous undo takes distinct entries
Simultaneous undo or redo requests from one person each apply a distinct entry of their stack exactly once, and the extras get the empty-stack 409.

Permission changes apply at once
A change to a member's role or row scope applies on that member's very next request in every existing session, and an open workspace whose scope narrows drops the hidden rows in place, closes any editor on them and announces how many rows are no longer shown.

Invite header safety
An email address carrying whitespace, control characters or header punctuation, or a document name carrying line breaks or control characters, is refused, and an invite's Subject is RFC 2047 encoded and folded as stated in Services when the document name is not plain ASCII.

Exports are stored snapshots, verified on download
A download serves the export's stored bytes only after re-verifying their size and SHA-256, unaffected by later edits, and a changed or missing object answers 502 export_corrupt with no file.

Collapsed means unavailable
The collapsed rail at 768 and the closed Tables drawer at 375 cannot be tabbed into, clicked or found by assistive technology.

Settle roll survives a new commit
A commit response arriving while an earlier roll plays ends that roll at its final values at once and leaves only the new commit's markers, badges, tally and sentence.

Safe return after sign-in
Signing in from a workspace link returns to that same-origin path, and any next value that is not a same-origin path lands on the documents list.

Responses applied in send order
The workspace applies commit, undo and redo responses in send order, so the newest-sent response decides the Undo and Redo state, alerts, markers and tally as stated in Interactions.

Request-scoped restricted views
Every restricted value, aggregate, summary group, count and recalculation list is computed inside the caller's own request and never carries another person's view, even under interleaved parallel requests.

Losing write access mid-session
A commit refused with 403 after a role change reverts like a failed commit, announces the permission copy and switches the workspace to read-only without a reload.

Cross-site requests refused
Every state-changing request, sign-in and sign-out included, that is identified as cross-site by its Origin or Fetch Metadata answers 403 cross_origin before session lookup and changes and sends nothing.

Abandoned exports and downloads released
A client that leaves mid-export or mid-download never leaves an export writing for more than 15 seconds, never blocks edits, and releases its database connection and storage stream.

Exports read one point in the edit order
Every export reads its table at one point in the document's edit order and never mixes cells from before and after one edit, and its record names its author and that document revision and never changes once ready or failed.

Export status, progress and announcements
The Export status message belongs to the newest Export CSV or Download press of the shown table, announces each writing, ready and failed change exactly once, survives list refreshes, commits and table switches, and its writing indicator follows reduced motion live.

Accessible names and read-only grid
The grid announces read-only for Viewers and announces the read-only notice once per write attempt without moving focus, rail and download links carry the exact names in Public screens and controls, and every error cell describes itself with its tooltip copy, which Escape hides without moving focus.

Contrast and not colour alone
All text including the pending value meets 4.5:1 on the ground, bars and focus outlines meet 3:1, and a refused field shows a message, an icon and an invalid state.

Row revisions and delete conflicts
Deleting a row carries the row's revision, so of a row delete and a cell write racing on one row exactly one succeeds and the other gets the 404 or 409 stated in Business rules.

Concurrent schema and data changes
A column rename racing a formula change, and a cell write racing its column's type change, resolve as one serial order with the exact outcome Business rules states for each order.

Table rename rewrites formulas
Renaming a table rewrites every formula token and summary name that names it, leaves every other character byte for byte, and one Undo restores the name and every text.

Cycle order and recovery
Cells of a cycle share one recalculation depth and order as stated in Business rules, the rest of the document keeps computing, and breaking the cycle recomputes those cells in the same request.

Document revision and edit history
Every committed edit raises the document revision by exactly one and adds one history entry in commit order, and refused or replayed requests add nothing.

Settled marker
The workspace carries the document revision of the newest applied response and a settled flag that turns true only after its Settle roll and tally finish.

Editing keys at the grid edges
While editing a cell, Enter, Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape commit or cancel and move the active cell exactly as stated in Interactions, including on the last row, last column and first column.

Counts current after rapid changes
Row counts, column counts, summary groups, formula results and stack counts in every edit response equal a fresh read, including after rapid successive edits, deletes and undos.

Settle roll phases
Every changed visible cell reports its waiting, rolling and settled phase, and a Decimal cell marks exactly its differing characters while rolling, on the depth timing stated in Motion and effects.

Range selection
Shift+Arrow and Shift+click select a rectangular range that can be copied as tab and CRLF text with a copy announcement, cleared as one undoable batch and filled by a one-cell paste, as stated in Interactions.

Idempotent commits
Every commit route replays a stored success for a repeated Idempotency-Key without applying the edit again and refuses a key reused for a different change, and the workspace resends a commit once with its key after a lost response, as stated in API, Business rules and Interactions.

Reference picker
Reference cells are picked from a keyboard-operable combobox and listbox that offers only visible, undeleted target rows read afresh at each opening, with the keys and copy in Interactions.

Access follows the newest response
The workspace's read-only state follows only the newest applied response that reports access, so a late earlier success, timers and list refreshes never re-enable editing, and a later read reporting Editor restores it without a reload.

Sign-in and sign-out landings
Sign-in, sign-out and Back after sign-out land on the published address with focus on the published control, and no document data is ever shown from history after sign-out.

Deleted-row status
Deleting a row shows the deleted-row status naming it with an Undo delete button for 8 seconds, paused while focused or hovered, whose Undo restores the row, focuses its cell and announces the restore once, and at 375 a long press on a card opens its row actions.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve and _schema run-manifest-v1, and serve runs the built app without a build step.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package with its name, version and licence, plus each bundled font and the icon set. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Shipped packages (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and bundled fonts use only the MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1 licences.
The app stores state only in Postgres and MinIO, sends mail only over SMTP, and uses no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or state files on disk.
The provided service definitions and dev credentials are used unchanged.
All server and browser source is TypeScript compiled with strict type checking turned on.
Fonts and icons are bundled and served from the app's own origin, and icons come only from Lucide.
